summary.intent: Run the security-review and crypto-privacy-review gates against the feat/engine-snapshot-and-read-surface branch (part of #802, CipherBox) after a code-simplify pass, to catch vulnerabilities before merging the snapshot/download read-path work spanning the Rust engine, wasm boundary, and TS client.
summary.outcome: Both review skills executed via subagents (security-review's vuln-identify → parallel false-positive-filter → confidence-threshold pipeline, and crypto-privacy-review against the project's AGENTS.md crypto rules); the crypto review surfaced issues that were then fixed by a follow-up agent in crates/engine/src/facade.rs, crates/engine/src/gate/floor.rs, and crates/engine/src/net/child.rs, and the fixes were committed and pushed.

repo: security-review skill structures its analysis as: (1) one subagent identifies candidate vulnerabilities across the full diff, (2) each candidate gets its own parallel subagent applying the FALSE POSITIVE FILTERING exclusion list and confidence scoring, (3) only findings scored 8+ survive into the final markdown report.

crypto-privacy-review skill checks changes against CipherBox's AGENTS.md security rules: no privateKey in localStorage/sessionStorage, no logging sensitive keys, no unencrypted keys sent to server, ECIES for key wrapping, AES-256-GCM for content encryption, TEE-only IPNS key decryption.

The engine's trust/adoption pipeline (child record adoption, floor laws, grant-section handling) is security-sensitive enough that crypto review findings landed specifically in crates/engine/src/facade.rs, crates/engine/src/gate/floor.rs, and crates/engine/src/net/child.rs — the ChildAdopter/floor-law/root-vs-child envelope trust boundary code from PR #802.
workflow: Large PR diffs (here 217KB) get persisted to a tool-results file with only a 2KB preview inlined rather than dumping the full diff into context — worth expecting when reviewing big branches.

friction: Full diff was too large to inline (217.2KB), requiring the reviewer to work from a truncated preview plus a persisted file reference rather than the complete diff in context.
open_items: The final markdown security-review report content (specific findings/severities) is not visible in this transcript excerpt — worth confirming what, if anything beyond the crypto-review fixes, was flagged and left unaddressed.
